target_customer: Veterinary clinics, hospital groups and individual veterinarians
problem: Veterinarians spend large amounts of time after visits writing clinical notes, which causes burnout and takes attention from patients.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per veterinarian, with a free trial
product_category: AI medical scribe and practice assistant for veterinary medicine

founders.name: Kevin Cohen
founders.background_notes: Originally from Venezuela. Five plus years building data and AI platforms at Microsoft, then blockchain data ingestion at Circle.

founders.name: David de Matheu
founders.background_notes: Six plus years at Microsoft on data and AI platforms and developer experience.

technical_complexity.rationale: Speech to structured SOAP notes with large language models was newly feasible in 2023 and needed veterinary templates and workflow integration, but relied on third party model APIs.

defensibility.rationale: Models were commodity APIs, so differentiation came from veterinary specific templates, integrations and security compliance (SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA claims on its site). Rivals could copy the core feature quickly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or incumbent takeover found. A competing scribe, ScribbleVet, was reportedly acquired by Instinct Science in January 2026 (single secondary source).

market_need_then: Documentation burden and burnout among veterinarians, described by the founders as coming from family and friends who were vets, plus the 2023 arrival of capable speech and language models.

identity.mascot_or_character: DAVID, a chat assistant (Diagnostic Assistant for Veterinary Insights and Differentials), is a product feature, not a mascot
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, benefit focused, relief for vets; uses superlatives such as 'the #1 AI-powered veterinary scribe' (company claim)

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that clearly signals its function, but no sourced evidence of community, merch or press about the brand itself. Partnerships (Cornell, Bond Vet, IndeVets, Ethos) show trust in the product more than the brand.

pivots.why: Founders had vets in their families and friends who struggled with notes; per the YC page they built developer AI tools for about five months first.

outcome_analysis: VetRec pivoted from developer AI tools into a veterinary scribe at the start of the 2023 generative AI wave and has expanded into intake, phone and an AI receptionist (July 2026) with named hospital group partnerships from 2024 to 2025. The company is active with a reported team of 45, but funding beyond aggregator-listed pre-seed money is not public, so its trajectory against a crowded scribe market is unproven.
notes: Funding: aggregators (vcbacked, PitchBook listing, CB Insights) report about 500K pre-seed around September 2023 with Y Combinator, possibly Orange Collective and Pioneer Fund. This rests on aggregators only, so it is unverified. Competitor list empty: searches found no sources dated near mid 2023; ScribbleVet, Talkatoo and Scribenote (8.2M seed Sept 2024) appear only in later pages. Team size 45 is from the dataset and YC page. Completeness pass: the $500K pre-seed is now recorded as a round (VCBacked and Caplight date it September 2023; PitchBook dates an accelerator entry 2023-07-31). It rests on databases only, with no company or press announcement. Investor names come from PitchBook and Caplight.
